statement: For an n x n square matrix A, the characteristic polynomial is the monic polynomial of degree n defined by p_A(t) = det(tI - A), whose roots are precisely the eigenvalues of A.

symbols.meaning: Square matrix representing a linear transformation
Non-zero eigenvector corresponding to eigenvalue λ
Eigenvalue scalar corresponding to eigenvector v
Dimension of the square matrix A

steps.text: For a linear transformation represented by a square matrix A, an eigenvector v and the corresponding eigenvalue λ satisfy the equation A v = λ v, with v ≠ 0.
Rewriting λ v as λ I v, the eigenvalue equation is equivalently expressed as (λ I - A) v = 0.
Because the eigenvector must be non-zero (v ≠ 0), the matrix (λ I - A) must be singular, which requires its determinant to vanish: det(λ I - A) = 0.

Replacing the scalar λ with an indeterminate variable t (or x), the eigenvalues of A are the roots of det(tI - A) = 0, which defines the characteristic polynomial p_A(t) = det(tI - A), a monic polynomial in t of degree n.

assumptions.assumption: A is a square matrix (n x n)
assumptions.breaks_when: A is rectangular (m x n with m ≠ n), making tI - A undefined and preventing determinant computation
v = 0, which trivially satisfies (λI - A)v = 0 for every λ and fails to force singularity of (λI - A)

assumptions.assumption: The scalar field is algebraically closed when full factorization into linear factors is required
assumptions.breaks_when: The matrix entries belong to a field that is not algebraically closed (such as the real numbers) and roots of p_A(t) lie in an extension field

failure_modes.signature: Matrix dimension mismatch in tI - A; determinant cannot be evaluated
failure_modes.cause: A has non-equal row and column dimensions (m ≠ n)

failure_modes.signature: Every scalar λ appears as a solution to A v = λ v
failure_modes.cause: v = 0 satisfies the linear equation for any λ without requiring det(λI - A) = 0

failure_modes.mode: Absence of eigenvalues in the base field
failure_modes.signature: p_A(t) has no roots or incomplete linear factorization over the base field
failure_modes.cause: The base field is not algebraically closed (e.g., real matrices with complex conjugate eigenvalues)
